claimOverrides.srs-objective: Choosing individuals from one numbered population list using random numbers avoids deliberate interviewer preference.
claimOverrides.srs-frame: Drawing individuals randomly from the full population requires a complete numbered list.

claimOverrides.strata-proportions: After randomly selecting individuals within each stratum, the planned sample proportions are maintained.
claimOverrides.strata-comparison: Random draws within each stratum provide planned coverage of important groups.
claimOverrides.quota-proportions: Non-random recruitment to fixed interviewer targets can reflect specified population group proportions.
claimOverrides.quota-no-frame: Filling predefined group targets by approaching available people does not require a complete population register.
claimOverrides.quota-comparison: Interviewers can recruit to stated group targets to include the chosen groups for comparison.

claimOverrides.quota-no-frame: Filling specified subgroup targets avoids needing a register of every eligible person.

claimOverrides.srs-objective: Generating a separate fair lottery of distinct unit labels avoids interviewer preference when selecting the fixed-size group.
claimOverrides.sys-speed: After calculating a fixed interval, an ordered list can be sampled quickly from one random start.
claimOverrides.srs-large: Generating and following up many separately selected random labels can be cumbersome for a large dispersed population.
claimOverrides.sys-noninteger: A fixed-step selection plan needs care when N/n is not a whole number; blindly rounding may give an incorrect count.

claimOverrides.srs-objective: Drawing distinct random unit labels from a complete numbered frame prevents deliberate interviewer choice at selection.
claimOverrides.quota-proportions: Setting fixed non-random recruitment targets by population subgroup can reflect chosen group proportions.
claimOverrides.quota-speed: Filling subgroup targets by approaching willing eligible people can be quicker than arranging separate random draws.
claimOverrides.srs-subgroups: An unstratified random draw may contain fewer people from a small important group than intended by chance.
claimOverrides.quota-unseen: Quota interviewers who replace refusals with nearby willing volunteers may hide nonresponse within a filled target.

claimOverrides.sys-single-start: An ordered list needs one random start; subsequent entries are selected at a fixed calculated interval.
claimOverrides.sys-frame: All eligible units must occupy identifiable positions in an ordered list so the fixed step can be followed.
claimOverrides.strata-proportions: Allocating places separately across defined strata prevents important groups being overlooked by chance.
claimOverrides.strata-random: After allocating places to each subgroup, random draws are still required within every stratum.
claimOverrides.strata-frames: For separate random selections, reliable sampling frames are needed for each of the classified population strata.

claimOverrides.strata-proportions: Random draws separately within fixed strata keep their planned proportions in the final sample.
claimOverrides.strata-frames: To choose randomly from each stratum, the relevant group lists must be reliably prepared.
claimOverrides.opp-easy: People immediately available at the chosen location can be recruited without a population lottery.
claimOverrides.opp-cost: Asking nearby willing respondents usually takes little time or money compared with making subgroup frames.
claimOverrides.opp-zero-frame: Choosing available eligible volunteers avoids both constructing a full random frame and setting subgroup targets.
